To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) model-based sparse component anlysis can be used to recover spatio-spectral components of speech signals from underdetermined convolved mixtures; (b) structured sparsity structures can be exploited to improve source localization and speech separation; (c) a large and randomly placed microphone array can be used to significantly improve source localization and separation; (d) the sparse Bayesian learning approach yields better perception quality while combinatorial optimization offers the most efficient computational complexity.

the sparse recovery algorithms are effective for speech source localization and that the performance of the algorithms can be significantly improved with the help of an average autoregression model and a block sparse structure.

(1) a sparse Bayesian learning method for source localization and separation outperforms the greedy and convex approaches; (2) the spatial sparsity structure of the acoustic image model enables the sparse reconstruction of speech signals with improved localization and separation; (3) the spectral sparsity structures of the speech signals enable improved localization and separation performance; (4) a large and random array of microphones enables improved localization and separation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formulation of a model-based sparse component decomposition framework for underdetermined source localization and separation of convolutive mixtures.
the development of a computational framework for model-based sparse component decomposition and its application to speech separation and localization.

model-based sparse component recovery for speech localization and separation from underdetermined convolved mixtures and we have shown the potential of exploiting structured sparsity for improved performance in terms of computational cost and perceptual quality.

model-based sparse component recovery is a viable and efficient framework for speech source localization and underdetermined separation from microphone array measurements.
the proposed model-based sparse component separation approach is able to achieve high quality speech separation and localization with a large and random deployment of the microphone array.
the model-based sparse component framework offers a powerful tool for source localization and separation of speech mixtures in a reverberating acoustic environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
model-based sparse component analyses exploiting the sparsity structures in the auditory and acoustic spaces can be successfully employed for underdetermined source localization and separation.
the model-based sparse component approach to underdetermined convlutive source localization and separation offers significant performance gains while being computationally tractable.
the proposed model-based sparse component framework is a promising approach for underdetermined speech source localization and source separation from microphone array recordings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the sparse recovery methods is significantly enhanced by incorporating the sparsity structures in both the spatial and spectral dimensions.

the model-based sparse component anlysis can be exploited to recover the source localization and separation information from underdetermined mixtured recordings of speech signals in reverberant acoustic environments.

model-based sparse recovery of the acoustic field is an attractive alternative to conventional beamforming and it can be used to design robust and efficient algorithms for source localization and separation in reverberant acoustic environments.
